note: The decision register. Each row states what is already known from an official source, what is still unknown, why it matters, the route to resolve it, the options, and what happens if it is never answered. 'blocking' means work downstream of it cannot be completed truthfully until it is answered. Nothing here is answered on the owner's behalf.
rows: Q-PRICE-01
PRICE
Where does the market price come from?
No market-price feed exists in this environment. The official NFL pages read this session publish results, schedules, injuries and venues - not prices.
Whether prices will be licensed from a vendor, taken from an exchange, self-captured from an operator, or not used at all.

Closing-line value, backtests, ROI, correlations of settled legs and every originated residual are all defined against a market price. Without one, none of them can be measured, which is why every edge field on this site is null.
Choose a source, then store one open/close pair per market before publishing any number.
A) licensed vendor feed; B) exchange/broker API; C) self-capture from one operator with written permission; D) research-only, no prices ever
D - the site stays a verified data and design layer and publishes no performance number
Q-PRICE-02
PRICE
What is the price-data policy?

NFL.com Terms section 1.3 permits use 'solely for your own individual non-commercial and informational purposes' and prohibits 'systematic retrieval of data or other content ... whether to create or compile, directly or indirectly, a collection, compilation, database, or directory' absent express prior written consent (page updated May 16, 2024).
Whether any nfl.com capture - including the injury and schedule captures already on this site - is retained, and under what storage model.
It decides whether the private data layer is required, what may be published, and what must stay off the public site.
Owner sets the policy field on the price-policy page; the site then enforces it.
A) derived analysis only, no raw retention; B) raw retained in a private store; C) raw retained with a written licence
A - the public site keeps derived analysis and links only; raw captures are removed from the repository
Q-PRICE-03
PRICE
How many settled legs are needed before a correlation is publishable?
A correlation coefficient is not a joint probability and not a causal effect. The register already requires n to be published with every value.
The minimum n, the clustering unit and the interval method.
Parlay and same-game-parlay pricing is invalid under dependence. Publishing a small-n correlation would manufacture a number that looks like permission to multiply marginals.
Reviewer sets the floor; the builder enforces it and refuses to render a value below it.
A) n>=300 settled legs, game-clustered bootstrap; B) n>=1000; C) never publish, use conservative bounds instead
A - n>=300 with the interval published alongside
Q-DEPTH-01
DEPTH
What is the authority for depth order?
The official injury report has no depth or replacement field. The official roster page does not publish a depth ordering.
Which source, verified club by club, establishes 1st/2nd/3rd/4th string.
Every deficiency feature on the brief - the matchup matrix, the per-team replacement view, the depth ablations, the staleness flag - is downstream of this one answer.
Evaluate the two named routes in order: (a) per-club official depth pages, verified club by club; (b) snap counts from an official source.
A) official club depth pages, verified 32/32; B) snap counts as the proxy; C) neither - publish absences only
C - the site names who is unavailable and never names a replacement
Q-DEPTH-02
DEPTH
What snap-share threshold makes a player a starter?
Snap counts are the named fallback starter proxy. The official Game Book PDFs are the identified source.
The numeric share, the minimum games, and how to treat a timeshare.
The threshold defines the label, so an unmeasured threshold would silently define the feature.
Set the number before any snap data is transcribed, then pre-register it.
A) highest snap share on the unit; B) >=50% of unit snaps; C) >=60%
A - rank by snap share within the unit, no absolute cut, with the value published per player
Q-ROSTER-01
ROSTER
Is there a dated official transactions and reserve-list source we may capture?
Roster turnover changes depth for weeks at a time, and a player on injured reserve produces no row on the weekly injury report at all.
The official URL for transactions and for reserve lists, and the capture terms for each.
Without it, 'not listed' is wrongly read as 'available', and depth rows go stale without any alarm.
Locate the official transactions and reserve pages, then add them to the capture job with a drift pin.
A) official transactions log captured daily; B) weekly only; C) not captured, absence typed as unknown
C - every absence from the report is typed 'unknown', never 'available'
Q-SNAPSHOT-01
SNAPSHOT
How often, and where, are availability snapshots stored?
One capture exists (2026-11-16). The official report is a live document, so a Friday capture and a Monday capture of the same week legitimately differ.
The capture cadence and the storage location.

The injury-as-surprise signal, the timestamped series, the weekly diff and the point-in-time ledger all need at least two observations of the same player-week. One capture makes every delta undefined.
Stand up a scheduled runner writing append-only, hash-stamped captures outside the static site.
A) Wed/Thu/Fri plus game day, private store; B) daily, private store; C) weekly only
C - deltas stay blank and the site states that one capture cannot support a surprise signal
Q-SNAPSHOT-02
SNAPSHOT
May prior-season weekly injury reports be archived?
The official injury report page offers a season selector going back to 1965.
Whether capturing and retaining historical weekly reports is permitted, and how far back.
Designation reliability (does 'Questionable' predict playing?) cannot be measured from a single week. This is the only route to that answer.
Read the applicable terms, then decide the archive window before capturing.
A) archive the current season only; B) archive 3 prior seasons; C) do not archive, and never use designation as a feature
C - designations stay labels and are never turned into probabilities
Q-BOOKS-01
BOOKS
May official Game Book PDFs be parsed and retained?
A Game Book PDF link is published on the official game centre for 12 of the 14 week 10 fixtures. Two fixtures had not been played or finished at capture time.
The terms for downloading, parsing and storing Game Book PDFs.
Game Books are the official source for actual starters, inactives and snap counts - which is the only non-inferred route to depth and to designation reliability.
Read the terms for static.nfl.com Game Book documents, then pre-register the parser before running it.
A) parse and keep derived fields only; B) parse and keep the PDFs; C) do not parse
C - no snap counts, no inactives, no actual starters; those columns stay blank
Q-STORE-01
GOVERNANCE
Where does durable storage live?
Raw captures currently sit inside the git repository that GitHub Pages publishes from.
The store, its retention policy and who can write to it.
Pages publishes everything in the repository root. Any data that should not be public is currently one commit away from being public.
Pick a store outside the published tree and add freshness and schema-change alerts.
A) private repository or object store with alerts; B) same repo, private submodule; C) leave it in the public tree
A - move raw captures out of the published tree; flagged as L-F-04 until done
Q-LEGAL-02
LEGAL
Is redistribution of any captured league data permitted?
NFL.com Terms section 1.3 was read and is quoted verbatim on the price-policy page. Sections 15-18 were not read this session.
Whether the derived tables published here are permitted, and in which jurisdiction.
It determines whether the public layer may publish row-level data at all, or only links and aggregate analysis.
Read the remaining terms sections and any applicable additional terms for the owner's jurisdiction, then set the public/private boundary.
A) public layer restricted to links and aggregates; B) public row-level permitted; C) legal review before any publication
A - the stricter boundary, applied now
Q-MODEL-03
MODEL
Which opponent-aware rating, and fitted on what?
148 verified FINAL 2026 games are ingested and split into train/validation/holdout.
The rating form, the features, and whether it is fitted at all before prices exist.
Ratings drive the originated side and total. Fitting before the split is frozen is how lookahead enters a backtest.
Pre-register the rating and the feature set, then fit on train and report on validation only until the holdout is used once.
A) simple score-differential rating with a home term; B) plus availability features once verified; C) do not fit yet
C - no rating value is published
Q-MODEL-04
MODEL
What are the 2026 kickoff and onside-kick priors?

The 2026 rulebook's change table states rule 6-1-6 'Permits the kicking team to declare an onside kick at any time during the game', 6-1-3 modifies receiving-team alignment in the setup zone, and 6-1-5 modifies the dead-ball spot after a touchback when the kickoff is from the 50.
The measured rates under the new regime.
Using pre-2026 kickoff and onside priors under a changed regime bises game totals and fourth-quarter comeback curves in one direction.
Measure from official 2026 results only, with n and an interval, and never mix pre-2026 seasons into the prior.
A) 2026-only prior with n published; B) pooled with a regime indicator; C) no prior, wider intervals instead
C - no regime prior is applied and the model carries wider uncertainty
Q-MODEL-05
MODEL
Is a within-season split acceptable as the holdout?
Only one season (2026) has been captured, so the train/validation/holdout split is necessarily inside that season.
Whether prior seasons will be captured so the holdout can be a whole season.
A within-season holdout leaks regime and roster context across folds; a season-level holdout does not.
Capture prior seasons' results, then re-split by season.
A) re-split by season once prior seasons are captured; B) keep the within-season split and publish the limitation; C) no holdout use until a season-level split exists
B - the within-season split is published with its limitation stated on the results page
Q-CORR-01
CORRELATION
Which combos may ever be ranked?
Multiplying marginal probabilities is invalid under dependence. The register requires a directly validated joint probability plus the operator's void and push rules.
Which specific combos will be measured, and which operator rules will be on file.
Same-game parlays and prop combos are exactly where dependence is largest and where a naive product looks most attractive.
Name the combos, measure the joint on settled data, and file the operator rules before ranking anything.
A) measure the named pairs only; B) allow any pair with n>=300; C) never rank combos
C - the combo divisions stay empty
Q-WX-01
WEATHER
Is there an official per-game stadium roof designation?
Venue and stadium are transcribed for all 14 week 10 fixtures. The National Weather Service is the designated official weather source.
Where the league publishes the roof designation, and whether an NWS gridpoint forecast can be pulled per kickoff with the terms checked.
Roof status and wind change totals and passing props. Guessing either is exactly the mispricing the requirement is written to prevent.
Locate the official roof designation source, then wire an NWS gridpoint pull per venue with a freshness alarm.
A) official roof designation + NWS hourly; B) NWS only, roof treated as unknown; C) no weather features
C - no weather value enters any model
Q-SCHED-02
SCHEDULE
Where is the league's dated schedule announcement?
The official 2026 schedule page is live and was read for weeks 1-10. It links to the flexible scheduling procedures for late-season changes.
A dated announcement page for the schedule itself.
Fixture-context features and the 'announced vs actual' fixture diff both need a dated baseline to diff against.
Locate and link the dated announcement; if none is published, record that as the finding.
A) link the dated announcement beside the live schedule; B) use the live schedule with its capture date; C) omit
C - field left blank and flagged as L-F-06
Q-GOV-01
GOVERNANCE
Who can approve a suggestion, and what does silence mean?
Every suggestion defaults to 'proposed' and nothing auto-approves on silence.
The named approver and the escalation rule.
Without a named approver a suggestion board is decoration; decisions get made by whoever edits a file last.
Name the approver in the site governance block.
A) single named approver; B) two-person rule for anything touching data capture; C) owner decides ad hoc
C - suggestions stay proposed
Q-GOV-02
GOVERNANCE
What numeric thresholds are the gates allowed to use?
Gate tests are mechanical and fail closed when a threshold is unset.
The sample floor for promotion, the demotion trigger values, the correlation floor and the CLV qualification bar.
A gate with a guessed threshold is not a gate; it is a number that launders variance into a decision.
Reviewer sets each threshold once, before any run, and the value is recorded with the commit that set it.
A) use the conservative defaults published on the leaderboard page; B) reviewer sets each one; C) leave unset and let the gates fail closed
C - gates fail closed and no strategy can be promoted
Q-RESULTS-02
RESULTS
May prior seasons' results be captured and retained?
2026 weeks 1-10 are captured: 148 FINAL games, each linked to its official game centre. The official schedule page offers a season selector covering earlier seasons.
Whether earlier seasons will be captured, how far back, and under what retention terms.
Prior seasons are what make a season-level train/validation/holdout split possible, and they are the only route to a kickoff-regime baseline that spans the 2026 rule change.
Answer Q-PRICE-02 and Q-STORE-01 first, since this is systematic capture of league pages; then capture season by season with a drift pin per page.
A) capture 2025 and 2024; B) capture five prior seasons; C) 2026 only
C - the split stays within 2026 and its limitation stays published (L-F-15)
Q-SCHED-01
SCHEDULE
Is the fixture-context capture run over the whole season or only the current week?
Venue and stadium are captured for all 14 week 10 fixtures. The official schedule pages for weeks 1-9 were read for results and byes.
Whether weeks 1-9 fixture context (venue, stadium, kickoff slot, international marker) is captured in the same shape as week 10.
Fixture-context features are currently computable for one week only, so any model using them has a one-week feature history and a ten-week result history.
Re-read the official schedule and game centre pages for weeks 1-9 in the same shape, with the same drift pins.
A) capture weeks 1-9 in the same shape; B) capture venue only, from the schedule page; C) leave it at week 10
C - the fixture-context columns stay populated for week 10 only
